name: smokeyp-codebase-mapper
description: Scan any repository and produce a polished HTML/PDF architecture report. Five architecture diagrams: a layered System Map hero (services and modules in frontend/backend/data tiers, HTTP calls bundled into per-service lanes), a Bertin module-dependency matrix, a C4 service-topology graph, a critical-paths swimlane, and a Sankey data-lineage view — each with data-derived architect observations and supporting small-multiples. Monorepo-aware module detection, broad HTTP framework coverage (NestJS, Express, FastAPI, Flask, Django, Rails, Spring Boot, Laravel, Go, Next.js), import parsing across Python/JS/TS/Go/Elixir (incl. workspace packages), ORM-driven data store mapping (Prisma, SQLAlchemy, Mongoose, Django ORM, ActiveRecord, JPA, Ecto), and beginner-friendly explainers throughout. Every quantitative section is product-scoped — vendored clones and dependency caches are excluded from the headline language/LOC, dependency, tier, and tree figures and shown separately as a secondary 'incl. dependencies' total, so the report measures your product, not its vendored code. An on-by-default LLM evaluation pass adds a code-derived overview, product-vs-vendored classification, and full-coverage cited execution flows — the scanner pre-computes one flow skeleton per HTTP route group and the LLM narrates each (use --no-llm to skip); module-graph edges and handler symbols are extracted with tree-sitter accuracy when the ast-grep binary is present (automatic, with full regex fallback). If the scanned repo already has a grepai semantic index (from the user's own grepai daemon), the evaluator uses it to ground findings; building an index is opt-in via --semantic. Self-contained core (Python stdlib only; ast-grep and grepai are optional accelerators), no JavaScript framework — the System Map and service topology add optional dependency-free focus interactions that degrade to complete static figures in print. Styled with the SmokeyP Labs 'Workshop' design system — a studio-grade field-report skin (photo masthead, numbered sections, machined detailing, inlined fonts) in light (default, print-safe) and dark (--theme dark) themes.
